statements.t: “The third quarter marked continued progress for ProKidney, with PROACT 1 advancing toward full enrollment and our pivotal eGFR slope topline readout remaining on track for the second quarter of 2027,” said Bruce Culleton, M.D., CEO of ProKidney.
The Company now expects total enrollment of over 500 subjects.

risks.t: the inability to maintain the listing of the Company’s Class A common stock on Nasdaq
the risk of downturns and a changing regulatory landscape in the highly competitive biotechnology industry
the risk that results of the Company’s clinical trials may not support approval
the risk that the FDA could require additional studies before approving the Company’s drug candidates
the Company’s need for additional financing and the inability of the Company to raise financing in the future
the inability of the Company to identify, in-license or acquire additional technology
the Company’s estimates regarding expenses, future revenue, capital requirements and needs for additional financing
the Company’s financial performance
the Company’s intellectual property rights
the fact that interim results from the Company’s clinical programs may not be indicative of future results
the impact of geopolitical conflict on the Company’s business

risks_dropped.t: the inability of Company to compete with other companies currently marketing or engaged in the biologics market and in the area of treatment of kidney diseases
the impact of geo-political conflict on the Company’s business
